analysis.investment_thesis: City Union Bank is a financial company — the Magic Formula explicitly excludes banks and financials because leverage is their raw material, not a capital structure choice, making EBIT/EV and ROIC meaningless. Even on bank-specific metrics, ROE of only 11.87% and revenue CAGR of 6.3% are uninspiring for a stock trading at 1.92x book.
key_strengths: Net profit has grown consistently: 760→937→1,016→1,124 Cr (FY22-FY25), CAGR of 13.9%
P/E of 15.3x and forward P/E of 12.5x offer modest valuation relative to large private banks
Strong institutional ownership (FII 23%, DII 41%) signals some confidence in the franchise
key_risks: ROE of 11.87% is well below the 15-18% I'd expect from a bank worth owning — cost of equity is likely higher than returns generated
Finance costs growing at 17.2% CAGR (FY22-FY25) while revenue grows at 6.3% — funding costs are outpacing earning assets
Revenue of 3,214 Cr on a market cap of 19,158 Cr gives P/S of 5.73x — expensive for a bank with mediocre ROE
red_flags: Magic Formula explicitly excludes financial institutions — EBIT/EV and ROIC are not applicable, removing this stock from the investable universe
Operating CF in 2024 dropped to only 436 Cr before recovering to 1,128 Cr in 2025 — lumpy cash generation raises questions about loan quality
analysis.detailed_analysis: Banks are structurally excluded from the Magic Formula because their balance sheets — funded predominantly by deposits and borrowings — make enterprise value and return on capital comparisons meaningless. CUB's 'operating margin' of 46% is a net interest spread metric, not an industrial EBIT. Evaluated on bank-specific terms: ROE of 11.87% is weak, total assets grew from 61,531 to 77,623 Cr (26% in 3 years) but equity only from 6,586 to 9,467 Cr, suggesting asset growth is outpacing capital generation. The bank is a mediocre regional franchise in a sector I simply can't rank using my framework.
